title: Edge-case review heuristics and follow-ups (PR mental model)
content:
Notes to self for reviewing PRs that touch runtime path and request routing. Goal: quick mental checklist, small test payloads, and concrete follow-ups. Keep short/iterative so I can paste into PR review comments.

High-level concerns (for any runtime PR):
- Backwards compatibility: does this change preserve existing wire behavior for older clients? Think: header names, optional fields, default values.
- Failure modes: what happens on RPC timeouts, OOM on GPU, kernel fallback? Is there a clear fallthrough path and metrics emitted?
- Observability: are spans/traces annotated with model_id, sequence_length, batching_slot? Are error codes stable?
- Performance regressions: is any hot path changed? run perf profiler on short/long sequences.

Edge-case test ideas (quick to run locally):
- Tiny token sequences (1-3 tokens) + long context prefix to exercise prefix cache path. Use deterministic seed to avoid sampling variability.
- Max-window warp: feed inputs at/just over supported sequence length (e.g., 2048 -> 2050) and verify graceful truncation or error.
- Interleaved streaming/early-exit: client closes stream mid‑generation -> ensure KV cache cleaned and no mem leak.
- Quantized-model fallback: run model with int4 profile and then intentionally corrupt a single weight byte (simulate bad quantization) -> ensure fallback to float path or clear error logged (do not ship silent corruption).
- Mixed-batch shapes: heterogeneous sequence_length within batch; ensure kernel selection doesn't assume uniform shapes and latency outliers are accounted.
- Metadata boundary: special characters in prompt/user_metadata (unicode, embedded JSON, very long strings) -> ensure sanitizer doesn't trim silently and metrics preserve length tag.

Code review checklist (concrete lines to look for):
- Any new public API? Validate docstring and update API compatibility matrix.
- Magic constants: replace with named constants + unit tests for boundary behavior.
- Thread-safety: look for shared mutable state accessed without locks (examples: global cache maps, static rng).
- Error wrapping: are errors enriched (with request id) before propagated to upper layers? Avoid swallowing.
- Tests: unit tests + small integration that run on CI GPU runner (cheap smoke) — if missing, request minimal repro test.
- Logging level: verbose debug logs gated with flags, not left at info for hot paths.

Follow-ups to add to backlog if reviewer +1s:
- Add a short harness to fuzz small/large sequence shapes across available kernels (ticket idea: FZ-110).
- Metric: add per-model "fallback_count" tagged by fallback_reason (quantization, missing kernel, OOM).
- Docs: short "How to simulate streaming client disconnects" runbook for SRE on-call.

Snippet prompts & payloads I reuse when testing (copy-paste):
- small-prefix: {"input":"Hi","max_tokens":5,"model":"rwkv-test"}
- long-prefix: {"input":"" + "A"*1900 + " end","max_tokens":10}
- mixed-batch: send 3 requests in batch shapes [8, 256, 1024] with same model/config
- unicode-stress: {"input":"Emoji: 😅🔥 — "quoted" 
 newlines","max_tokens":20}

Typical review comments I leave (short templates):
- "Nit: move magic number X to named constant + doc comment on choice. (reason: boundary tests)"
- "Can you add a unit test that exercises the [edge] code path? A minimal JSON payload and expected side-effect is fine."
- "Observability: please emit request_id + model_id in the error path and add a quick test that asserts presence."
- "Risk: this changes hot path in serving loop. Please run perf tag: short-run (1k requests, mixed shapes) and paste numbers."

Unresolved questions to ask authors (quick checklist):
- Did you consider existing batching heuristics? If not, why is this change required now?
- Are there compatibility guarantees we are relying on for enterprise customers (header names, response format)?
- What is the intended fallback strategy on unsupported hardware kernels?

Personal post-review TODOs (so I don't forget):
- If merged, add a temporary alert for 'fallback_count > 0' for first 48 hours post-deploy.
- Schedule 15m with author to walk topology changes if they touch routing or shard placement.
- Add example to runtime docs showing how to force fallback locally.

Finish: keep this doc short and iterate. I tend to copy relevant sections into PR comments. When I encounter a new recurring edge-case, add a tiny test or a ticket rather than relying on comments alone.

-- Ashwin
